persona.name: Gerard Fontaine

occupation.title: Retired SNCF Train Conductor
occupation.organization: Retired after 38 years with SNCF, based out of Dijon
occupation.description: Spent four decades on the Paris-Lyon-Mediterranee corridor and now fills his days with the garden, the grandkids on Wednesdays, and the association of retired railway workers. His wife Josiane still works part-time at the pharmacy counter, so weekday lunches are, to everyone's surprise including his own, his department now.

persona.education: Technical baccalaureate, then SNCF's internal training system — he'll tell you the railway was his university.
long_term_goals: Stay healthy enough to walk the vineyards route every autumn
Teach the grandkids to fish at the Lac Kir
Finally organize forty years of railway photographs
Keep Josiane laughing, which he considers his main pension obligation
persona.style: Amiable and unhurried, with a storyteller's timing honed on decades of platform announcements. Agreeable in conversation but almost immovable in habit — he'll nod along with your new idea and then do exactly what he did last Tuesday. Cardigan, cap, Ouest-France under the arm. New services neither excite nor offend him; they simply concern a world he feels politely exempt from.

traits: Easygoing and sociable in his circle

interests: His vegetable garden and two apricot trees
Regional cycling on flat roads only
likes: Boeuf bourguignon that took the afternoon
The Halles market on Saturday with Josiane
A small glass of Marsannay with cheese
dislikes: Food that arrives in a box with instructions
Paying monthly for anything he could do himself
Being rushed, by anyone, for any reason

beliefs: A garden and a good butcher cover most of life's menu
Habits aren't ruts, they're rails — they get you there on time
You help family with your hands, not with gadgets
Lunch is an institution, not an interruption
skills: Slow-simmered Burgundy classics, three of them, excellent
Fixing bicycles and most household objects
Making a two-hour lunch feel efficient

general: Cooks the same rotation of simple lunches weekdays, proudly
Saturday market at the Halles, list in Josiane's handwriting
Pays in cash or cheque; the bank card is for the autoroute
Delegates all novelty decisions to Josiane and his daughter

morning: 6h30 wake without an alarm — forty years of shifts left their mark
workday: Garden or association mornings, errands on foot
Lunch at 12h15 sharp, then a 20-minute nap he denies taking
evening: Dinner with Josiane at 19h30, soup-based half the year
Regional news, a documentary, bed by 22h
weekend: Saturday: Halles market, boules or fishing
Sunday: the big family lunch — his bourguignon or his son-in-law's barbecue

health.physical: Solid for 66 — garden-fit; type 2 diabetes managed with medication and Josiane's supervision of his dessert habits.
health.mental: Content and unbothered; misses the camaraderie of the depot more than the work.

relationships.name: Josiane Fontaine
relationships.description: Part-time pharmacy assistant, the household's minister of innovation — anything new in the house arrived because Josiane decided so, and the meal kit question will be no different.

relationships.name: Celine
relationships.description: A hospital administrator in Dijon whose two kids spend Wednesdays with him; she worries her parents eat 'too heavy' and keeps suggesting modern solutions he politely files away.

relationships.name: Roger
relationships.description: Former colleague and boules rival; their Thursday debates cover pensions, tomatoes, and the general decline of everything, cheerfully.
